limitations: This is the existing agent(prompt, {profileVersionId}) worker selector, not invocation of a complete published agent or its saved workflow.

Absent policy preserves legacy grant-based worker selection; it does not authorize future published-agent invocation. New agents created through the administrative UI default to an explicit empty allowlist.
The root own pinned version remains eligible as an implementation worker. Each other exact version needs both policy inclusion and current execution-owner grants.
Publication validates unique UUID references, at most 128. Unknown, disabled and inaccessible targets fail when selected; publication does not grant access.
Constrained Qwen tool/MCP invocation and delegation ancestry/depth/concurrency/call budgets remain P4 work.
Docker uses stock Qwen and a deterministic model fixture, not corporate harness authorization.
verificationNotes: Real migrated SQLite covers selection, direct binding admission, current dispatch authority, foreign-user denial, target revocation/regrant, same-profile different-version denial and immutable root policy after republication.
The existing workflow service rechecks profile resolution for cached results, retry and replay; worker dispatch also checks its saved parent policy through core lineage validation.
Native Docker published workflow fixtures now opt into explicit policies for both users, and separately assert a granted target outside an empty policy fails without creating a worker binding.

The production browser creates an agent with the allowlist and republishes it through the real admin API. Browser-only fixture additions run from the host during the composite; product changes and native fixtures were included in the tested image.
